articles.title_orig: How the Jensen Huang affair changes the outlook for U.S.-China relations
articles.title_zh: How the Jensen Huang affair changes the outlook for U.S.-China relations
articles.content_orig:
BEIJING — Prolonged U.S. Congressional scrutiny of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises the stakes for already tense relations between the world's two largest economies.
Nvidia's Huang resigned Thursday, and agreed to testify before Congress sometime before Thanksgiving on Nov. 26. House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast, R-Fla., told reporters there could be "public hearings for other people or other things down road."
"I worry this incident will deteriorate the atmosphere dramatically in Washington against China, and also export control matters, and also the Trump administration in its way of dealing with China," said a Beijing-based foreign policy researcher, who requested anonymity as academics risk discipline or even removal for speaking to the media.
The researcher warned of a possible return to a situation like that in the 1990s, when a " Chinese-American " nuclear physicist was suspected of sharing nuclear secrets with the Chinese government , resulting in a federal prosecution . The court ultimately dismissed all but one of 59 counts.
Now the bilateral relationship, supported by a fragile trade truce, faces another espionage allegation . And this time it's around the tech executive at the heart of the U.S.-China competition over artificial intelligence.
"This isn't really about Jensen," said Mitch Presnick, non-resident honorary fellow on the Chinese economy, Center for China Analysis at the Asia Society.
He noted how some in Washington prefer measures to exclude China and disagreed with the semiconductor executive's message that American technology needed to be used in China in order to remain relevant to global tech development.
Washington started to restrict Nvidia's ability to sell advanced chips to China in 2022. But the Trump administration eased many Biden-era restrictions in 2025.
Meanwhile, Nvidia's Huang advocated his views across a spectrum of markets from the U.S. to China to Taiwan to Germany.
At the peak of his influence, he shared a banquet table in September with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit in Washington, D.C. The two presidents are next expected to meet alongside the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting from Nov. 18 to 19 in Shenzhen, China.
The political landscape has swiftly changed, with Democrats sweeping U.S. midterm elections on Nov. 3 and turmoil over subsequent reports about Huang's alleged Beijing spy connection. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair over the weekend.
It remains unclear whether any sensitive information was shared.
China's Foreign Ministry has called the "Chinese spy" allegation unfounded " smears against China. "
"The U.S. should stop fabricating the "Chinese spy" narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions," spokeswoman Mao Ning said Thursday, according to an official English translation .
But the immediate outcome, analysts predict, is more of the U.S. restrictions that China doesn't want.
"The Nvidia scandal has destroyed the credibility of the biggest corporate lobbyist against U.S. export controls on China," said Arthur Kroeber, partner, Gavekal Dragonomics. "There is now a good chance that Congress will tighten up those rules before the end of this year."
Looking ahead, Kroeber warned Beijing could cut off supplies of rare earths or chipmaking materials if the U.S. tried to restrict China further with the MATCH Act or Affiliates Rule. The measures could, respectively, limit Beijing's access to key tech suppliers in the Netherlands and Japan, and drastically expand export controls to include many subsidiaries.
"So when Trump and Xi meet next week in Shenzhen they will probably agree to keep the uneasy U.S.-China truce going," Kroeber said. "It will just keep getting more and more uneasy."
Pressuring China has been a rare area of bipartisan agreement in Washington. Beijing has meanwhile ramped up homegrown alternatives to U.S. tech since Washington restricted Nvidia's ability to sell advanced chips to China in 2022. And even Trump's approval of some Nvidia sales had yet to translate into meaningful orders from China.
"We are going to see the two countries start to decouple again in terms of technology," George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice, The Asia Group, said Thursday, noting "China will double-down on self-reliance."
"I begin to feel the Jensen Huang case feels like more like another 'spy balloon' case ," he said.
In early 2023, during the Biden administration, the U.S. shot down what it described as a Chinese surveillance balloon. Beijing called it a weather balloon that had blown off course. But the incident delayed then-U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken's trip to China by more than four months, following limited engagement amid Covid-19 travel restrictions.
Fast-forward to the Huang affair, and "the timing is no accident here," Presnick said. "We're talking about a very curious set of coincidences, and also the fact that the information came through unnamed sources, and there were other things that were strange about it."
Days after the U.S. midterms, The Financial Times and The New York Times reported, citing sources, that U.S. government intelligence believe China's Ministry of State Security recruited businesswoman Alice Huang to gather information on then-CEO of Nvidia Jensen Huang.
"Obviously somebody was looking to do this, and they wanted to ... make the discussion about espionage, and not about American competitiveness," Presnick said.
"The U.S. is thinking [in terms of] U.S. and China, but that's not what China is thinking," he said, pointing to Beijing's trade with fast-growing non-Western economies in Africa and Southeast Asia.
—CNBC's Samantha Subin contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: After meeting Putin, U.S. envoys say Europe to join talks on ending Ukraine war
articles.title_zh: After meeting Putin, U.S. envoys say Europe to join talks on ending Ukraine war
articles.content_orig:
Russian president says he would target any foreign troops sent to Ukraine and refuses to soften territorial demands
Vladimir Putin warned US negotiators that Russia would target any foreign troops deployed to Ukraine, in a series of hardline remarks that came as the Ukrainian military faced renewed disruptions to Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service.
During the talks at the Kremlin with the US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on Thursday, the Russian president refused to soften his territorial demands, insisting on full control over four Ukrainian regions that Moscow claims to have annexed.
He also ruled out accepting the deployment of foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine , describing such a move as a “continuation of war”.
Putin’s comments appeared to severely dampen hopes that a peace deal could be within reach, after Volodymyr Zelenskyy said there was a “window of opportunity” to reach an agreement before the end of 2026.
The latest trip to Moscow by Witkoff and Kushner, who have made numerous visits to Russia, was partly aimed at securing European participation in future negotiations, according to two people familiar with the talks.
Speaking after the meeting, Witkoff confirmed that European representatives would join the next round of talks. “They’re our partners, and it’s important for them to be involved,” he told reporters as he boarded a plane leaving Moscow.
The US envoys will now travel to Dublin, Ireland, where they will meet Zelenskyy and debrief him on the Moscow meeting.
Andy Burnham, the British prime minister, said national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the talks in Berlin.
Amid a flurry of diplomatic activity, including the recent talks in Abu Dhabi, the Kremlin appears to have succeeded in reframing negotiations over the war in Ukraine as part of a broader discussion about European security.
But Europe is wary of Russian attempts to focus discussions on a European security architecture, while Moscow continues to pound Ukraine with bombs and missiles.
The EU foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told reporters: “We already have a European security architecture in place.” Kallas pointed to the cold war-era Helsinki accords and the Budapest memorandum , which guaranteed the territorial integrity of Ukraine. “The problem is that Russia is not keeping to those agreements, so right now the focus should be that Russia actually keeps to their obligations … and they don’t attack another country again.” Focusing on a European security architecture was a “distraction” without a ceasefire, she added.
Both Washington and Moscow have been urging European leaders to appoint a single representative to lead negotiations on their behalf.
“Once a representative is appointed, a chief negotiator authorised to speak on Europe’s behalf, there will be a four-way dialogue,” Putin said on Thursday.
EU leaders are due to discuss the issue of who speaks for Europe on Friday, but so far have declined to nominate one person to speak for the bloc. One EU official said the EU would be represented by its institutions when issues concerning the union were on the table, but played down any imminent appointment. They said: “Do I expect an agreement on a special representative? My answer is no, I don’t.”
Kallas suggested she – as the EU’s high representative for foreign and security policy – should represent the EU in talks, alongside António Costa, the president of the European Council.
More than 45 European leaders are meeting in Dublin for the European Political Community summit, a gathering that brings together nearly every country on the continent, apart from the leaders of Belarus and Russia.
The French president, Emmanuel Macron, played down the importance of having a single European negotiator, saying “the content determines the format”. “There is no more US support. So there [are] some mediations, fine,” he said, referring to the process led by Kushner and Witkoff. “But at the end of the day we will be the one to define and decide for our future security as Europeans.”
The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, said it was first necessary to get Putin to the negotiating table before deciding on a European envoy. Merz said: “It’s not about individuals. What matters is that Putin is prepared to hold talks.”
Meanwhile, Zelenskyy accused Musk’s Starlink satellite service of damaging Ukraine’s ability to defend itself against Russian drone attacks, after Ukrainian military officials reported new restrictions on the system.
According to Zelenskyy, Starshield, a military version of Starlink funded by the Pentagon, has for several days been subject to speed limits of 100mph (161km/h) along the frontline and in Russian-occupied territory.
Similar restrictions last month prompted confusion over who had ordered them, with Musk and the Trump administration pointing fingers at each other before the service was partly restored.
The latest restrictions had made it harder for Ukrainian forces to intercept Russia’s increasingly sophisticated jet-powered drones, Zelenskyy said, accusing the service of “helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine”.
Kyiv has contacted Washington to seek an explanation for the disruption, which Zelenskyy said appeared to be deliberate rather than a technical fault.

articles.title_orig: Democrats Open Probe Into Trump’s Deal to Export Nvidia Chips to China
articles.title_zh: Democrats Open Probe Into Trump’s Deal to Export Nvidia Chips to China
articles.content_orig:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire by critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang contributed to the federal agency's lack of oversight over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS has learned.
Before President Trump nominated Lutnick to lead the Commerce Department, Lutnick was the chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, a New York investment bank which held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time.
Lutnick developed a warm relationship with Huang, who resigned Thursday as reports of a growing number of affairs caused new uncertainty about the world's dominant AI chipmaker. One of Huang's alleged relationships was with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang), who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy. She ran Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that became one of Nvidia's biggest customers for AI chips and is suspected of illegally shipping Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to Chinese entities, circumventing a U.S. ban.
As commerce secretary, Lutnick took the helm of an agency responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals.
One way the Commerce Department keeps this information and technology out of the hands of China and other adversaries is by putting foreign companies and individuals on its Entity List . This restricts their ability to access U.S. technology products, and inclusion on the list means that the department believes there's a risk that the entity is involved in activities that are contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.
In 2024, under the Biden administration, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security launched an investigation into Nvidia's chip sales to Megaspeed to determine whether they were being redirected to China. But according to The New York Times , the probe was abruptly transferred to the Department of Justice. The Justice Department would not comment about the investigation.
The Commerce Department has not added a company to the Entity List since October 2025.
Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over the Commerce Department's failure to place Megaspeed on the Entity List, Axios reported.
Chris McGuire, an expert on China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said, "The real scandal here is the lack of enforcement of export controls."
He added that the Commerce Department had known for as long as a year that Megaspeed was being run by a woman who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy, "and they did nothing." The New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang.
"Either Lutnick doesn't know how to do his job or he is protecting Huang," McGuire said.
The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
On Thursday, after Jensen Huang's resignation became public, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, called on Lutnick and his deputy, Jeffrey Kessler, to "explain why they have not closed export control loopholes." Kessler is the undersecretary who led the Commerce Department's probe into Megaspeed.
Warren urged the two to "act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In March, Warren wrote to Lutnick to demand the "immediate pausing" of all export licenses of Nvidia chips destined for China.
Questions about Lutnick's own relationship with Chinese state companies have further complicated the ongoing Nvidia crisis.
A financial services firm Lutnick ran, BGC Group, had a 33% stake in a joint venture with China Credit Trust, a Chinese state-owned company whose largest shareholder is the China People's Insurance Company, another state enterprise.
Another firm he ran, Cantor Fitzgerald, is still overseen by his two eldest sons. That firm helped several Chinese companies go public in the U.S. Cantor Fitzgerald was also a key investor in Satellogic, a satellite company that is under contract with a Chinese data science company, Zhong Ke Guang Qi Space, until 2033.
His close China ties emerged as a topic at his Senate confirmation hearing last year. Senators questioned whether he could be unduly influenced by Chinese officials, and how he would safeguard U.S. technology.
Sen. Maria Cantwell, a Democrat from Washington state, grilled Lutnick on potential conflicts of interest with respect to his investments in Chinese companies, and Cantor Fitzgerald's financial interest in Tether, a cryptocurrency company with a large footprint in China.
Other senators asked about how he would safeguard U.S. technology from the Chinese Communist Party.
"How will you address different threats that we see coming from the CCP within these information and technology markets?" asked GOP Sen. Deb Fischer, of Nebraska.
Lutnick promised to be vigilant against threats from China.
"I take a very jaundiced view of China," he said in response to Fischer. "I think they only care about themselves and seek harm to us, and so we need to protect ourselves."
Before he was sworn in as commerce secretary in February 2025, Lutnick resigned from all of his corporate leadership posts, transferring his business empire to his children.
Since his tenure as commerce secretary began, Lutnick and his family's net worth doubled to $7.3 billion, thanks to his indirect stake in Tether, according to Forbes , which valued his holding in Tether at $5.4 billion. The stake, worth $1.7 billion in early 2025, has more than tripled in value.
"Can we be confident that he is looking out for the public interest?" asked Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "What's going on with him raises a lot of red flags."
Lutnick's friendship with Jensen Huang may also be problematic, Clark told CBS News.
Huang met Lutnick soon after Lutnick began his term as commerce secretary, Huang told podcaster Joe Rogan last year.
"He started our conversation with, 'Jensen, this is Secretary Lutnick,'" said Huang. "'I just want to let you know that you're a national treasure. Nvidia is a national treasure. And whenever you need access to the president, the administration, you call us.'"
Huang added that every time he called the commerce secretary's office, "if I want to get something off my chest, express some concern, they're always available."
Huang also visited with President Trump. He attended a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025. At that time, Huang tried to convince Mr. Trump to lift restrictions on the company's less advanced H20 chip sales to China, according to The New York Times . Less than three months later, in July 2025, Mr. Trump lifted the restrictions. Nvidia's most advanced chip, the Blackwell, still cannot be sold directly to China.
In July 2025, Lutnick posted a photo to Instagram showing Huang in his trademark black leather jacket standing in the Oval Office next to Mr. Trump, who was seated at his desk. Lutnick is also in the photo along with other visitors.
"Great to meet in the Oval Office with Jensen Huang on the very day Nvidia crossed $4 trillion in market cap," the post said.

articles.title_orig: Rare Earth Wars U.S. General Sounds Alarm Over China's Military Leverage
articles.title_zh: Rare Earth Wars U.S. General Sounds Alarm Over China's Military Leverage
articles.content_orig:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday after the G7 Foreign Ministers' meeting in Paris, that "bad things are happening to the Iranian economy and it's unfortunate."
The U.S. Air Force abruptly relocated more than a dozen aircraft from RAF Mildenhall in eastern England amid an emerging security threat, U.S. officials confirmed Tuesday.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the move, citing sources who said the threat originated in Iran.
As U.S. officials assessed the threat's nature and urgency, commanders raised the base's security level to Force Protection Condition Charlie, the military's second-highest alert level, indicating a likely terrorist threat against personnel or facilities.
IRAN HAS 'SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED' EFFORTS TO TARGET AMERICANS ABROAD, US INTELLIGENCE MEMO WARNS
U.S. Air Force KC-135, used for in-flight refueling, takes off from RAF Mildenhall Airbase. (AP Photo/Max Nash, File)
Flight-tracking data and open-source analysts with the Military Air Tracking Alliance identified 13 U.S. aircraft leaving the base late Monday, the Associated Press said.
Nine Boeing KC-135 Stratotankers were moved to airfields in Scotland, Germany and Spain.
Three CV-22B Ospreys were relocated to nearby RAF Lakenheath, which has hardened aircraft shelters.
A U.S. official told The Associated Press the moves were precautionary, noting that some aircraft were on rotational deployments while others were permanently stationed in the United Kingdom .
IRAN UNDER SCRUTINY AFTER PLOT FOILED NEAR UK BASE USED BY US MILITARY
American aircrews check a B-52 Stratofortress long-range subsonic bomber aircraft on the pan at RAF Fairford. The United Kingdom reportedly is refusing to let the United States use the base for a potential attack on Iran. (Getty Images)
The move marks the second major relocation of U.S. military aircraft from Britain in less than two months.
In early October, the Air Force pulled heavy bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire after British counterterrorism police stopped three suspicious vans headed toward the base Sept. 27.
Two men have since been charged under the United Kingdom's National Security Act.
Separately, the Justice Department unsealed indictments against three Iranian-backed operatives on Tuesday accused of involvement in coordinated terrorist plots across Europe, including RAF Fairford.
UK POLICE ARREST 'EXPLOSIVE' SUSPECTS NEAR US AIRBASE, KEY TO IRAN WAR
The main gate of RAF Fairford is pictured on September 27, 2026 in Fairford, United Kingdom. Police declared a major incident after evacuating residents from their homes in Whelford, a village about one mile from RAF Fairford, a military base that hosts U.S. Air Force bombers involved in the Iran conflict. (David Bown/Getty Images)
RAF Mildenhall is home to the 100th Air Refueling Wing, the only permanently based U.S. tanker wing in Europe.
Its KC-135 Stratotankers support allied aerial refueling and long-range strike missions across the region.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday that Washington routinely repositions military forces.
"We are constantly repositioning forces around the world for a variety of reasons," Rubio told reporters when asked about the evacuation.

A 10 Downing Street spokesperson said British air bases remain secure and that London and Washington continuously share intelligence on potential threats.
Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title_orig: What to Expect From Best Buy's 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sales
articles.title_zh: What to Expect From Best Buy's 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sales
articles.content_orig:
For all intents and purposes, Black Friday sales are already here. There are plenty of deals out already, even though we're weeks away from the actual event. One of the reasons for that is the competition retailers have with each other to be the first to get your money. One of the retailers that is making the biggest early splash is Best Buy , confirming their entire plan for the rest of the year. Here's what you need to know.
Best Buy has announced the following events:
DoorBoosters : A Halloween sale from Oct. 30 to Nov. 1.
Early Black Friday Deals and Doorbusters: The official start of early Black Friday deals on Nov. 6. New deals will drop every Friday.
Black Friday Doorbusters and Deals : Best Buy says this will be its main sale, starting on Thursday, Nov. 19 and running until Nov. 28 with deals on "computing, gaming, home theater, wearables, and more."
Cyber Sunday and Monday : Best Buy is extending Cyber Monday to five days and says you can find deals going up to 50% off select tech.
Last-minute savings : The Christmas sale will run from Dec. 18 until Dec. 24.
You don't need to be any kind of member to shop Best Buy's Black Friday in July sale; however, it is free to sign up for a My Best Buy membership , which will get you free shipping. If you join one of their paid subscriptions (My Best Buy Plus for $49.99 per year or My Best Buy Total for $179.99 per year), you'll get faster free shipping, exclusive prices and deals, an extended 60-day return window on most products, and access to select sales, like the Member Deals Days sale that is going on right now. Paid members will also earn extra rewards from both the current sale and the upcoming Black Friday in July sale.
You can find deals on TVs, laptops, headphones, video games, electric bikes, and more. There will be new deals every week in stores, on its website, and in the Best Buy mobile app . They'll offer price matching, meaning if the price drops further during the sale (Dec. 24), they will match it and offer a refund.
Here are the best deals I've found so far. I'll be updating these deals throughout the sale, so make sure to come back and see what's new. Remember that new deals drop every day.
Best Buy price matches its own products, so if a product drops in price later, you'd get those savings too, but it does not cover any deals coming from a competitor's Black Friday sale. There are some other important exceptions you can read in more detail here .
In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.
The other major retailers doing Black Friday sales are Amazon , Target , and Walmart . Currently, Amazon has many early deals, seeing their lowest prices yet. Target has some week-long deals and a Deal of the Day. Walmart will have three Black Friday and Cyber Monday shopping events. Nowadays, large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026.
No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

articles.title_orig: Megaspeed ex-CEO Alice Huang barred from Singapore amid Nvidia saga
articles.title_zh: Megaspeed ex-CEO Alice Huang barred from Singapore amid Nvidia saga
articles.content_orig:
President Trump suggested on Thursday that Tim Cook, former CEO of Apple, should become the leader of chip maker Nvidia following its chief executive Jensen Huang ’s resignation over his alleged affairs with two women.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! ” Trump posted on TruthSocial.
Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on Thursday morning, in the wake of reports that he had allegedly been involved in two affairs, including one with a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy.
It is unclear if Trump has reached out to Cook regarding this suggestion. TIME has reached out to the White House for comment.
Huang and the White House have maintained a close relationship since the start of Trump’s second term. During his official visit to China in May, Trump invited Huang to attend the summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The New York Times reported that the President insisted on inviting Huang to join the delegation despite concerns over Huang’s relationship with a woman who is believed to be a Chinese spy.
Speaking with reporters on Monday, Trump repeatedly downplayed Huang’s alleged affair, insisting that he believed the tech billionaire’s assertion that he knew nothing about the alleged espionage operation.
“I really believe him,” Trump told reporters during the White House press conference. “I think that he’ll be in good shape.”

articles.title_orig: Trump Had Urged Nvidia’s Jensen Huang to Fight for His Job
articles.title_zh: Trump Had Urged Nvidia’s Jensen Huang to Fight for His Job
articles.content_orig:
Some Nvidia employees are calling for Jensen Huang’s return even after his multiple reported extramarital affairs and abrupt resignation , according to internal correspondence reviewed by WIRED.
An internal “suggestion box” post submitted before Huang’s resignation by a longtime engineer at Nvidia urged the company’s board to take employee sentiment into consideration prior to taking any action. The submission has attracted more than 1,600 comments since then, with several asking board members to find a way to bring back Huang.
“If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss,” wrote one anonymous commenter.
“We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance,” wrote another.
One employee went as far as sending a companywide email demanding transparency into Huang’s exit. “I stand by Jensen,” the staffer wrote. “Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us.”
The employee couldn’t be reached for comment, while the engineer behind the suggestion box post declined to comment.
Nvidia and its new board chair, investor Harvey Jones, didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment.
Huang, a 63-year-old who had led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, wrote in an email to employees on Sunday that he had been “unfaithful to [his] wife” and that there was “no excuse.” The acknowledgement followed reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset . The board announced Huang’s resignation on Thursday morning, following reports of an alleged second affair with a direct report. (This employee has not commented on the matter.) Since then, Reuters reported on an alleged affair with yet another Nvidia employee. Huang hasn’t commented about these reports since his Sunday email.
Nvidia’s board is largely made up of early Nvidia investors and Huang’s longtime confidants. It named Nvidia chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO , and former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones as chair of the board. The crisis has cost the company $1 trillion in market value since the allegations surfaced, prompted investigations from US lawmakers and the FBI, and raised the prospect of new export controls on chips.
It’s been business as usual inside the company throughout this week, but Huang’s resignation left many employees stunned . In the hours after, about two dozen employees posted on LinkedIn in support of Huang, with one describing their faith in his leadership as unwavering. Over the same period, WIRED couldn’t identify any posts from Nvidia employees in support of his resignation.
Many employees had expected a board investigation to conclude before any big changes would occur. For instance, the suggestion box post called on the board to share its findings with employees and formally solicit their sentiment “about Jensen’s continuing as our CEO.”
Instead, Huang left just as the inquiry had begun. Staffers are seeking to better understand why. “If America fails the man who helped build its future,” the employee in the companywide email stated, “then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang.”

articles.title_orig: Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3
articles.title_zh: Xbox announces Wolfenstein 3
articles.content_orig:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed a new entry in the Wolfenstein series with a brief tease.
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed a new entry in the Wolfenstein series with a brief tease.
It’s been nearly a decade since Bethesda’s MachineGames released Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus in 2017, and now Xbox is ready to announce a sequel from the studio. Wolfenstein 3 was officially announced today, just days after Bethesda also confirmed that the next Elder Scrolls game will be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel .
In a post, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced the name and a photo of a script. “Looking forward to sharing more,” she said . MachineGames also announced the game in a post , saying the game is “in production” and sharing a photo from a motion-capture session. IGN reports that Brian Bloom (who plays protagonist William Joseph “BJ” Blazkowicz) and Debra Wilson (who plays Grace Walker) are reprising their roles, and they appear to be the featured actors in the photo.
The last mainline entry, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus , launched in 2017 and continued the story of Blazkowicz in an alternate 1960s where Nazi Germany had won the Second World War. Wolfenstein: Youngblood also debuted in 2019 as a co-op spinoff, starring Blazkowicz’s twin daughters.

articles.title_orig: Was This New Fable Gameplay Meant to Sell the Game?
articles.title_zh: Was This New Fable Gameplay Meant to Sell the Game?
articles.content_orig:
I am pretty confident Fable will be a fantastic RPG when it finally releases in February 2027, but for those still sat on the fence, Xbox is going to have to do a better job of promoting it than this latest example.
To mark the 25th anniversary of Xbox, four minutes of gameplay taken from a quest has been uploaded. However, all of maybe 30 seconds of it actually has anything going on. Watch it above.
Obviously, you do indeed do a lot of walking during open world RPGs, but it's not something you usually feature much in marketing beats. That's what most of the latest gameplay slice for Fable is, though: walking.
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
Partway through, there is a combat sequence showing off swordfighting, archery, and magical abilities. It's over quickly, however, and then we're back to walking. The video then concludes with a cutscene lacking context as it's been plucked out of the full game to be seen online.
I grew up playing the three mainline Fable games on the Original Xbox and Xbox 360; I have very fond memories of this series, so I want the new rebooted instalment to do well. It'll need better presentations and trailers than this for a good chance at that. It's out for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC on 23rd February 2027.
What do you make of the video? Share your thoughts in the comments below.
Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.
I am sure that this going to be a good game
I am very excited for Fable but I must admit the combat always looked janky since they first showed it off.
Edit: also going to throw this out there, First party Sony games get stick for having slow walking section... just an observation
Yeah, I think they couldve chosen a more exciting part of the game to highlight. It’d be like the Spider-Man 2028 trailers featuring clips of Peter walking about FEAST.
The combat section looked really good here I thought. Why did they want to show off that the game has a load of walking in it?
Looks boring and don't tell me that's the fastest you can run. Can't sprint?
It's probably meant to be a graphical showcase and narrative tease. Doesn't mean it's good — and, more than anything, it was probably thrown together in a few days because daddy Microsoft abruptly told them to make a trailer for Xbox's anniversary.
But...I dunno. I wouldn't give them too much flack for it. I certainly wasn't aware of this trailer before reading this article, so I doubt it has much gravitas to it or is intended to sell the game to a wide audience. Just some subpar marketing from the studio that is pretty bad at marketing.
All I can assume is it’s an attempt to be a graphical showcase. Which doesn’t do much for me because it’s so much less stylised than previous games in the series and looks more like a new Hellblade than a new Fable. I dunno, I still don’t think the general tone of that headline would be the same if this was a PS exclusive and not an Xbox game. Do we remember the GoT trailer during a state of play that was like 6 or 7 minutes of walking before any combat?
I just have that feeling it’s not going to be all that. I’m just doing my Zelda OOT play through and watched the fable trailer. Unfortunately the trailer did absolutely nothing for me compared to what I was playing and enemies I was fighting and combat in OOT. Apart from FH6 I don’t think their studios are capable for whatever reason of producing a game of OOT quality etc.
@RoomWithaMoose you nailed it. Definitely a last minute "trailer". They've already shown all they need to, and this trailer doesn't do any help nor harm at this point. That being said, it still looks good to me ,and I'm stoked for the return of Fable proper after all these years.
It looks like a technical demo that should have stayed in-house and should never have been used to showcase the game for a public presentation. I'm still going to play the game.
Why do Xbox studios games of late environments look so static. Gears e day was like it and fable seems the same. No areas where there are trees and bushes blowing in the hard wind, rain lashing down, soaking wet floors, massive snow falls, you get the idea. Gears and fable environmentally look ok but dull very slight breeze and very minimal object foliage movement etc in all areas.
Did you not know? Xbox pioneered walking in video games!
But seriously, I'm just gonna ignore that this video was even put out. Every game has slow sections, it can't be all flashy set pieces and bombastic action, especially in a narrative-driven RPG. I'll just wait to see more gameplay and the reviews when they come out at launch.
Yeah not a great showing this, I agree. Although overall I'm still looking forward to the game.
@AI-Generation also replaying OoT and forgot how seminal and sublime it is. I’m not sure many are capable of producing something like that even 28 years after the OG came out!
Im sure the full game will be great, I'm genuinely looking forward to it. But that trailer really gave me some DA Veilguard vibes and thats not a great thing :/
As others have said, I think this was meant to be a graphical showcase. I’m sure they’ll be a “gameplay” trailer closer to release. My most anticipated game even over GTA VI!!!
The game isn't out for another 3 months so I'm sure they'll cook up more gameplay videos by then.
Glaring at Bethesda At least they showed SOMETHING.
Still looking forward to it
Reminded me of the majority of the GoW Laufey reveal. I don’t get why games continue to get showed off like this nowadays when graphical improvements are giving diminishing returns, made much more sense over a decade ago certain games would be a clear graphical leap.
Liam, come on man. Is this an article for clickbait. The Sony MS war is over. Sony won. There are many other videos of the gameplay. Why stir the flames for your crowd? Can people get over the console wars at this point?
You just know even after every Sony misstep, at the end of the day, they walk into the last conference room for the night and go ‘still, at least we aren’t Xbox.’ And have a good laugh.
I'm still gonna buy it 'cause I like what I see so far and that it's gonna be my first ever Fable game since I've never owned an Xbox
Not the best showcase for the game. I want to believe for this one, but I’m waiting to see how the game reviews before I jump on it.
None of the fables ever rose above good so unlike the author of the article I do not expect this to be a fantastic rpg not even a little
@UnfishedPlate29 yeah if you ignored all the combat Laufey showed off in that 20 mins

The Claude developer plans to price its shares Nov. 18 and begin trading the following day. articles.title_orig: White House weighs Commerce Secretary Lutnick's ouster amid Nvidia export concerns, sources say
articles.title_zh: White House weighs Commerce Secretary Lutnick's ouster amid Nvidia export concerns, sources say
articles.content_orig:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire by critics asking whether his ties to Chinese companies and friendship with Nvidia's ousted CEO Jensen Huang contributed to the federal agency's lack of oversight over billions in Nvidia AI chip sales, CBS has learned.
Before President Trump nominated Lutnick to lead the Commerce Department, Lutnick was the chairman and CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, a New York investment bank which held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock at the time.
Lutnick developed a warm relationship with Huang, who resigned Thursday as reports of a growing number of affairs caused new uncertainty about the world's dominant AI chipmaker. One of Huang's alleged relationships was with Alice Huang (no relation to Jensen Huang), who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy. She ran Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based company that became one of Nvidia's biggest customers for AI chips and is suspected of illegally shipping Nvidia's most advanced AI chips to Chinese entities, circumventing a U.S. ban.
As commerce secretary, Lutnick took the helm of an agency responsible for policing exports of sensitive technology to adversaries and global rivals.
One way the Commerce Department keeps this information and technology out of the hands of China and other adversaries is by putting foreign companies and individuals on its Entity List . This restricts their ability to access U.S. technology products, and inclusion on the list means that the department believes there's a risk that the entity is involved in activities that are contrary to U.S. national security or foreign policy interests.
In 2024, under the Biden administration, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security launched an investigation into Nvidia's chip sales to Megaspeed to determine whether they were being redirected to China. But according to The New York Times , the probe was abruptly transferred to the Department of Justice. The Justice Department would not comment about the investigation.
The Commerce Department has not added a company to the Entity List since October 2025.
Last week, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick over the Commerce Department's failure to place Megaspeed on the Entity List, Axios reported.
Chris McGuire, an expert on China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said, "The real scandal here is the lack of enforcement of export controls."
He added that the Commerce Department had known for as long as a year that Megaspeed was being run by a woman who is believed by the U.S. to be a Chinese spy, "and they did nothing." The New York Times reported that about a year ago, President Trump was briefed on intelligence that suggested that Alice Huang was a Chinese asset and that she had grown close to Jensen Huang.
"Either Lutnick doesn't know how to do his job or he is protecting Huang," McGuire said.
The Commerce Department did not respond to a request for comment.
On Thursday, after Jensen Huang's resignation became public, Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, called on Lutnick and his deputy, Jeffrey Kessler, to "explain why they have not closed export control loopholes." Kessler is the undersecretary who led the Commerce Department's probe into Megaspeed.
Warren urged the two to "act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In March, Warren wrote to Lutnick to demand the "immediate pausing" of all export licenses of Nvidia chips destined for China.
Questions about Lutnick's own relationship with Chinese state companies have further complicated the ongoing Nvidia crisis.
A financial services firm Lutnick ran, BGC Group, had a 33% stake in a joint venture with China Credit Trust, a Chinese state-owned company whose largest shareholder is the China People's Insurance Company, another state enterprise.
Another firm he ran, Cantor Fitzgerald, is still overseen by his two eldest sons. That firm helped several Chinese companies go public in the U.S. Cantor Fitzgerald was also a key investor in Satellogic, a satellite company that is under contract with a Chinese data science company, Zhong Ke Guang Qi Space, until 2033.
His close China ties emerged as a topic at his Senate confirmation hearing last year. Senators questioned whether he could be unduly influenced by Chinese officials, and how he would safeguard U.S. technology.
Sen. Maria Cantwell, a Democrat from Washington state, grilled Lutnick on potential conflicts of interest with respect to his investments in Chinese companies, and Cantor Fitzgerald's financial interest in Tether, a cryptocurrency company with a large footprint in China.
Other senators asked about how he would safeguard U.S. technology from the Chinese Communist Party.
"How will you address different threats that we see coming from the CCP within these information and technology markets?" asked GOP Sen. Deb Fischer, of Nebraska.
Lutnick promised to be vigilant against threats from China.
"I take a very jaundiced view of China," he said in response to Fischer. "I think they only care about themselves and seek harm to us, and so we need to protect ourselves."
Before he was sworn in as commerce secretary in February 2025, Lutnick resigned from all of his corporate leadership posts, transferring his business empire to his children.
Since his tenure as commerce secretary began, Lutnick and his family's net worth doubled to $7.3 billion, thanks to his indirect stake in Tether, according to Forbes , which valued his holding in Tether at $5.4 billion. The stake, worth $1.7 billion in early 2025, has more than tripled in value.
"Can we be confident that he is looking out for the public interest?" asked Kathleen Clark, a law professor and expert on government ethics at Washington University in St. Louis. "What's going on with him raises a lot of red flags."
Lutnick's friendship with Jensen Huang may also be problematic, Clark told CBS News.
Huang met Lutnick soon after Lutnick began his term as commerce secretary, Huang told podcaster Joe Rogan last year.
"He started our conversation with, 'Jensen, this is Secretary Lutnick,'" said Huang. "'I just want to let you know that you're a national treasure. Nvidia is a national treasure. And whenever you need access to the president, the administration, you call us.'"
Huang added that every time he called the commerce secretary's office, "if I want to get something off my chest, express some concern, they're always available."
Huang also visited with President Trump. He attended a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025. At that time, Huang tried to convince Mr. Trump to lift restrictions on the company's less advanced H20 chip sales to China, according to The New York Times . Less than three months later, in July 2025, Mr. Trump lifted the restrictions. Nvidia's most advanced chip, the Blackwell, still cannot be sold directly to China.
In July 2025, Lutnick posted a photo to Instagram showing Huang in his trademark black leather jacket standing in the Oval Office next to Mr. Trump, who was seated at his desk. Lutnick is also in the photo along with other visitors.
"Great to meet in the Oval Office with Jensen Huang on the very day Nvidia crossed $4 trillion in market cap," the post said.

articles.title_orig: Newsom blasts Trump’s climate retreat as giving China an edge
articles.title_zh: Newsom blasts Trump’s climate retreat as giving China an edge
articles.content_orig:
Gov. Gavin Newsom blasted President Trump’s retreat from the fight against climate change, casting it as a global embarrassment and a squandered opportunity to make domestic manufacturing gains.
“China is cleaning our clock,” Newsom said on the sidelines of the United Nations-backed climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkey. “It’s not just about environmental policy. It’s about influence, it’s about supply chains, it’s about investment. As we walk off the international stage, they’re stepping in, and they’re also stepping in with this new technology.”
Newsom, a potential Democratic contender for the U.S. presidency in 2028, was joined by a phalanx of other governors and mayors at the COP31 summit Thursday. Their presence at the talks was a show of force meant to illustrate the work that cities and states are still doing to decarbonize following the Trump administration’s rollback of emission-limiting regulations and withdrawal from the Paris Agreement.
The U.S. government didn’t send an official delegation to the high-level talks, which have brought together nearly 200 countries. Instead, the country was represented unofficially by other U.S. officials. On Thursday, the group included U.S. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz, New Mexico Gov. Michelle Lujan Grisham and a number of mayors. A coalition of some 19 U.S. House representatives also are set to participate later this week.
Newsom, however, was by far the most visible representative of the U.S., mobbed by dozens of reporters, activists and onlookers as he inched slowly through the venue Thursday, occasionally stopping for selfies and winning the same kind of acclaim showered earlier in the week on Brazil’s newly reelected President Lula da Silva. “We love you, Governor Newsom,” shouted one observer. “You must be president!” yelled another.
U.S. representatives at the climate talks said they were buoyed by the U.S. midterm elections last week, which ushered Democrats into control of the House and Senate as well as a majority of state governorships.
“We’re doing all of this in our states with no help from Washington,” Walz said, adding that Democratic control of Congress could help facilitate those efforts. Under Trump, the federal government has been “throwing barriers into place,” he said, but “it’ll be very difficult for them to do that now.”
Newsom also said he felt “renewed optimism from the midterms” but remained concerned about two more years of environmental policy under Trump. Democrats can wield fresh power to mitigate “the damage,” he said, but can only go so far.
“Trump’s head is in sand soaked with oil. He’s a wholly-owned subsidiary of big oil and we have been on the receiving end of some of the most aggressive assaults on our climate leadership in our generation,” Newsom said.
During Trump’s second term, the administration has pulled back a host of Biden-era regulations, including a mix of mandates and subsidies that encouraged electric vehicles. That’s imperiling American competitiveness, Newsom said.
“I worry about American automobile manufacturers surviving a decade from now,” Newsom said. “If you care about the future of American manufacturing and of automobile manufacturing, you should care about this issue. And so that’s the message I’m communicating here in the absence of one damn representative from the federal government. We are a footnote yet again at COP and that is a disgrace.”
Leaders of cities and states representing more than 60% of the U.S. economy have used the summit to pledge they’d keep forging forward on climate —including by formally collaborating with United Nations officials in tracking the country’s greenhouse gas emissions.
That pledge came in a joint statement from America Is All In, the U.S. Climate Alliance and Climate Mayors initiatives. Collectively, they represent 24 governors with constituents making up 55% of the U.S. population as well as 350 mayors across 47 states.
The two-week COP31 summit is meant to galvanize a worldwide shift away from fossil fuels, an embrace of more emission-free renewable alternatives and additional conservation efforts. The alliances of state and local leaders committed to working with the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, the treaty and institution undergirding the 2015 Paris accord, without support from the U.S. government. Under a formal process kicked off this year, the U.S. is set to officially exit the UNFCCC next February.
The new effort by cities, states and other leaders will involve elevating data on U.S. progress toward decarbonization by midcentury and ensuring engagement in a “global stocktake” exercise meant to assess how the world is doing in meeting its climate goals. A first global stocktake culminated in 2023 with a recognition the world was badly off track its key temperature target, prompting a pledge at COP29 in Dubai to transition away from fossil fuels. articles.title_orig: Cramer says Jensen Huang betrayed Nvidia shareholders. How to pick up the pieces
articles.title_zh: Cramer says Jensen Huang betrayed Nvidia shareholders. How to pick up the pieces
articles.content_orig:
CNBC's Jim Cramer criticized former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Thursday for putting the chipmaker's future at risk.
"Did he betray you, the shareholders?" Cramer asked. "Yes. End of story."
Huang resigned Thursday morning following reports of an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Hours later, Reuters reported that he had an "intimate relationship" with a second employee. These revelations came days after Huang admitted to an affair with an executive at a Singapore-based cloud computing company whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China. Longtime CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO of Nvidia. Cramer said Huang's departure was necessary to protect Nvidia from further fallout.
Shares ended Thursday down more than 4%, but at its lows of the morning, the stock was off over 14%. The decline in Thursday's session brings Nvidia's losses this year to 12%.
While questions remain about what comes next for the AI chipmaker, Cramer argued that Nvidia's future extends beyond the executive who helped build it into one of the world's most valuable companies. "There won't be a better Nvidia, just a different one [without Huang]," Cramer said, envisioning a company that is better organized and more disciplined about its investments.
Under Huang, Nvidia built an extensive equity investment portfolio that included a $5 billion investment in Intel in 2025 and a $2 billion investment in AI cloud provider CoreWeave earlier this year. The investments, and many others, were part of Huang's strategy to strengthen Nvidia's position across the AI industry.
During the CNBC Investing Club's Morning Meeting livestream Thursday, Cramer recalled urging Kress to reduce the company's stakes in Intel and CoreWeave, only to be told that Huang preferred to maintain them. Cramer suggested that new leadership could take a more disciplined approach to capital allocation, potentially cashing in on some of those investments and returning the proceeds to shareholders through even bigger stock buybacks.
Cramer expressed confidence in Kress, praising her deep understanding of Nvidia's operations and financials. He argued that the longtime finance chief is well positioned to provide stability as the company navigates the investigations surrounding Huang, which stretch from the boardroom to Washington, D.C.
Nvidia didn't respond to CNBC's request for comment on Cramer's remarks. Heller, the crisis PR firm Huang reportedly hired as early as last year, did not respond to CNBC's request for comment.
Going forward, Nvidia's underlying business remains strong, Cramer said, pointing to its substantial cash reserves and expectations for a robust earnings report Tuesday evening. But he cautioned that even strong quarterly results might not be enough to reassure investors during this time of lingering uncertainty.
Investigations into Huang's conduct and possible violations of U.S. chip export restrictions could result in sanctions that hurt Nvidia's international business. Meanwhile, competitors, including Advanced Micro Devices , are making progress with their own AI chips, potentially threatening Nvidia's market dominance. AMD shares surged almost 6% on Thursday, extending their winning streak to five straight sessions.
Those risks have prompted Cramer to take a more cautious approach to Nvidia stock , particularly after the substantial gains shares have delivered over the years for Cramer's Charitable Trust , the portfolio of 32 stocks managed by the Club. On Tuesday, as Huang's future at Nvidia looked more and more in doubt, the Club downgraded Nvidia to a hold-equivalent rating.
"Don't ever turn a successful investment into an unsuccessful trade," he said, urging longtime shareholders sitting on big gains to consider taking some profits. "You don't want to give up all of your gains if the stock falls further. It fell further today after many of the analysts jumped ship and downgraded the stock from buy to hold. There could be more ahead."
At the same time, Cramer cautioned against giving up on Nvidia altogether, pointing to the company's extensive engineering expertise and multiyear product roadmap as reasons to believe it can continue competing at the forefront of AI without Huang.
The "Mad Money" host also drew parallels to Apple's leadership transition from Steve Jobs to Tim Cook , suggesting that Nvidia could benefit from a similarly capable successor who brings a different management style without sacrificing the company's technological edge.

U.S. Treasury yields jumped on Thursday, with the 10-year note yield surging above 5%, alongside a move higher in oil prices and expectations of further Federal Reserve hikes.
The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — rose more than 13 basis points to 5.125%.
The 2-year Treasury note yield, more sensitive to short-term Fed interest rate decisions, jumped more than 15 basis points to 4.879%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury bond yield rose 10 basis points to 5.449%.
One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another.
The rise in oil prices came after President Donald Trump said, " We don't need a deal with Iran ," raising concern that the war in the Middle East will continue indefinitely. West Texas Intermediate futures gained more than 2% to close at $88.74 per barrel, while Brent crude was ahead more than 3% to $95.82 per barrel.
Tuesday's hotter-than-expected consumer price index reading has investors anticipating more rate increases from the Fed. Goldman Sachs added another rate hike to its forecast on Wednesday, now expecting an additional quarter percentage point increase in March.
Traders are pricing in 100% odds of an increase in December, with the chance of a half percentage point increase standing at about 13%, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool.
Another inflation report is due Friday, when the October producer price index, which tracks wholesale prices, is expected to show a 0.4% rise in October, down from the 1.3% surge in September.
On Thursday, investors looked to October's home sales report from the National Association of Realtors, which showed that existing home sales reached their lowest level in more than 16 years last month .
"Fed officials want to push rates even higher to fight inflation, but all this is doing is pushing the housing correction down into the depths of depression," said Chris Rupkey, FWDBONDS chief economist. "It's dark out there with no homebuyers anywhere to be found."

articles.title_orig: Chabad Rov Faces Calls for Criminal Investigation Over Psak
articles.title_zh: Chabad Rov Faces Calls for Criminal Investigation Over Psak
articles.content_orig:
ב׳ כסלו ה׳תשפ״ז | November 12, 2026
An Israeli left-wing lawmaker called for a criminal investigation into Harav Gedalia Axelrod, following a psak he issued concerning the formation of an Israeli government supported by Arab political parties.
An Israeli lawmaker from the left-wing “Democrats” party has called for a criminal investigation into Harav Gedalia Axelrod , a senior Chabad rov and former Av Beis Din of Chaifa, following a halachic ruling he issued concerning the formation of an Israeli government supported by Arab political parties.
MK Michal Rozin called on Thursday for authorities to investigate Harav Axelrod, accusing him of incitement to violence and racism over a letter he published earlier this week.
In the letter, Harav Axelrod warned against establishing a government with the participation or support of Arab parties, ruling that political leaders who facilitate such a government fall under the halachic category one whose actions endanger the lives of others.
He further warned that lawmakers who allow such a government to be formed by abstaining from a vote would also bear responsibility for endangering Jewish lives.
Rozin responded on X, claiming that the rov’s statements crossed the line from religious expression into criminal incitement.
She drew comparisons to the period leading up to the 1995 assassination of Israeli Prime Minister Yitzchak Rabin , warning that similar rhetoric directed at political leaders had preceded acts of violence.
The controversy comes amid statements by Democrats chairman Yair Golan , who has advocated forming a government with the participation of Arab parties. Golan has also called for ending what he describes as a “racist separation” between Jewish and Arab votes when determining which political bloc can form a government.
Following the publication of Harav Axelrod’s letter, the Center for Victims of Racism filed an urgent complaint with Israel Police, the Attorney General, and the State Attorney’s Office, demanding an investigation into possible offenses of incitement to violence, solicitation of murder, and incitement to racism.
The calls for criminal proceedings against the 85-year-old veteran rov drew criticism from the Israeli civil rights organization B’Tsalmo.
Its director, Shai Glick , accused left-wing politicians and organizations of attempting to silence rabbonim through the threat of criminal prosecution.
“The Knesset has barely begun, and the silencing has already started,” Glick said.
He called on prosecutors to dismiss the complaint, arguing that rabbonim and public figures should not face criminal prosecution merely for expressing their religious and halachic positions.
In response to the controversy, Chabad spokesman Rabbi Shimi Segal clarified that Harav Axelrod’s statements do not represent Chabad’s official position.
“Chabad’s official halachic positions are determined exclusively by the Chabad Rabbinical Court, in accordance with the Rebbe’s instructions,” he said. “Rabbi Axelrod is not a member of the court and does not hold a leadership position in Chabad. His statements and letters reflect his personal views alone.”

articles.title_orig: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket ties
articles.title_zh: Kalshi ends Donald Trump Jr. advisory role over Polymarket ties
articles.content_orig:
Kalshi, the nation’s leading prediction market, said on Thursday that Donald Trump Jr., the president’s eldest son, would no longer serve as an adviser.
The firm’s officials said in a statement that they and Donald Trump Jr. had agreed to part ways because his investment firm, 1789, had heavily invested in Polymarket, Kalshi’s biggest competitor. A spokesman for Donald Trump Jr. confirmed that the decision was mutual.
It was not immediately clear whether the president’s oldest son would keep the shares in Kalshi given to him as part of his compensation package when it hired him in January 2025. Those assets are now estimated to be worth millions.
Kalshi said it reached out to Donald Trump Jr. this fall to discuss ending his contract after 1789, in August, added about $300 million to its investments in Polymarket on top of its earlier contributions of about $200 million.
“Both parties understood that advising two competitors in a growing sector was complicating things,” the company said in a statement. Kalshi’s decision was reported earlier Thursday by Reuters.
The Trump administration has been a huge booster of prediction markets. After sweeping the midterm elections, Democrats in Congress have promised to investigate allegations of self-dealing by the administration. Some critics have pointed to federal regulatory approvals given to Kalshi as a prime example of the administration’s conflicts of interest.
Most recently, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which regulates prediction markets, authorized Kalshi to offer a type of trading on stocks, cryptocurrencies and other assets without owning them, which had not been allowed before in the United States. Those decisions, starting in May, prompted highly unusual lawsuits from major trading clearinghouses, claiming that the C.F.T.C. was violating federal laws designed to protect investors and financial markets.
The administration has also taken on both red and blue states that claim Kalshi and other prediction markets are subject to state regulations and laws governing sports betting. The C.F.T.C. has taken the opposite view, backing Kalshi in a slew of lawsuits with the states. Donald Trump Jr. echoed the C.F.T.C.’s stance in a closed-door meeting with Republican state attorneys general in March.
Through his spokesman, the president’s son has previously said he was involved only in helping Kalshi market itself, not in negotiating with the federal government.
Sharon LaFraniere is an investigative reporter focusing on the Trump administration.

articles.title_orig: What’s a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
articles.title_zh: What’s a Honey Trap? The spy tactic that helped topple Jensen Huang
articles.content_orig:
A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (in black) at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan on May 22, 2025. CTI via Reuters hide caption
One of the world's oldest spy tactics appears to have helped topple one of the world's richest men. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday amid revelations that he had an affair with a female client that U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy, according to the New York Times.
NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting by the Times, which said Huang also had an unrelated affair with a company executive who reported to him. The Chinese government has called the accusation of spying, "nothing but smears against China."
Using a romantic relationship to gather intelligence from foreigners – known as a honey trap – has a long history in China and beyond. The Chinese Ministry of State Security, the country's main civilian intelligence agency, routinely tries to recruit women and occasionally men for honey traps, according to former CIA officers and other U.S. officials familiar with Chinese spy craft.
Some target businessmen for industrial espionage or to gain insights into the economic and political strategy of foreign governments. Peter Mattis , a former CIA counter-intelligence analyst, said honey traps also serve as influence operations with spies trying to gain enough trust to shape the target's thinking about China.
"The biggest thing here that we should pay attention to is that the Ministry of State Security celebrates a tradition of getting inside the enemy's decision-making," said Mattis, president of the Jamestown Foundation , a national security think tank in Washington, D.C., that focuses on America's geopolitical rivals.
Nicholas Eftimiades , who spent more than 34 years with the CIA and Defense Intelligence Agency and now teaches at Penn State, said the honey trap is just one tactic among many that use ordinary Chinese citizens to gather information at home and abroad.
"Unlike the CIA, or MI6 or any of the other Western services, China has a 'whole of society approach,'" said Eftimiades, the author of Chinese Intelligence Operations: An Analysis of the People's Republic of China's Intelligence Services. "Chinese law supports this. The National Intelligence Law of 2017 requires citizens to cooperate with intelligence collection efforts."
The Chinese government has employed honey traps in the United States and elsewhere in the West. In the 2010s, Christine Fang worked as a political fundraiser in California where she developed a physical relationship with Democrat Rep. Eric Swalwell before and after he became a congressman.
The FBI warned Swalwell they thought Fang was a spy. He denied doing anything wrong and she fled back to China.
In the 1980s and 1990s, the FBI paid Katrina Leung – a Los Angeles businesswoman – $1.7 million over 18 years to spy on China. However, Leung had affairs with two FBI agents and the bureau later determined she was a double-agent.
The most remarkable honey trap case dates to the 1960s, when a young French diplomat began a nearly two-decade affair with a male Peking opera performer, whom he thought was a woman. The story inspired the play and movie, M Butterfly .
The woman implicated in the Nvidia case, Alice Huang, is a Chinese businesswoman whose company, Megaspeed, was a major buyer of advanced chips from Nvidia. The Times reported the U.S. had her under surveillance and learned of her connections to Chinese state security through her communications.
The logo of data center company Megaspeed International is pictured at its office in the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore on November 10, 2026. The woman accused of spying for China during an affair with Jensen Huang, head of US artificial intelligence chip titan Nvidia, has been named in media reports as tech executive Alice Huang, who has reportedly been a top figure at Singapore-based company. Taryn Ng/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
Desmond Shum, a Hong Kong businessman and former China insider, says Alice Huang doesn't fit the usual profile in these cases. She appears to be what the Chinese call a "white glove" – or front-person for multi-billion-dollar commercial deals, which Shum says could have insulated her from the Ministry of State Security.
Shum doesn't think Alice Huang is a professional spy, pointing out that she hasn't been discreet on social media, posting photos from her visits to luxurious country clubs and fancy foreign destinations.
"A spy wouldn't do that," Shum told NPR from his home in the United Kingdom.
Isaac Stone Fish , a former reporter in China who runs Strategy Risks, a China-focused business intelligence firm, says the Ministry of State Security – or MSS – could have approached Alice Huang after it learned of her affair with the Nvidia head.
"One imagines that every time a Chinese person enters into a romantic relationship with a very, very powerful American, MSS notices that," Stone Fish said.
Honey traps are a staple of spy novel and movie plots, including the Netflix series, Black Doves , The Americans on FX, Apple TV's Slow Horses as well as James Bond films, such as From Russia with Love .
In reality, when Chinese state security approaches women for these operations, it's embarrassing and humiliating. The tactic perpetuates racist, sexist stereotypes while casting suspicion on the vast majority of Chinese people, who have nothing to do with intelligence gathering.
In addition to China, many intelligence services have engaged in honey traps. The Russians historically used sex workers for blackmail and leverage. During the Cold-War, East Germany sent well-educated and well-mannered male spies – known as Romeos – to West Germany.
Mossad, the Israeli intelligence service, used honey traps from the 1950s into the 1970s in countries such as Egypt, Iraq and Iran. But investigative reporter Yossi Melman, who's written many books on Israeli intelligence, says the practice has dwindled as cyber spying and digital traps have proven more efficient.
The U.S. used sexual entrapment against the Soviets, but several former officials said the Americans now prefer to appeal to people on ideological grounds and provide financial carrots, such as money for college tuition or health care for a sick family member.
Even though countries repeatedly warn businessmen and government officials about the tell-tale signs of a honey trap, ego and vanity remain human weaknesses and men continue to succumb, said Eftimiades.
"Welcome to the male of the species," he said. "Is everyone aware of this? Yes. Does everyone think it'll happen to them? No. And, you know, and it happens all the time."
